identity.title: Evidence of a Flat Outer Rotation Curve in a Star-bursting Disk Galaxy at z = 1.6

paper_type_evidence.quote: The data were obtained with the Multi-Object Spectrometer For Infra-Red Exploration (MOSFIRE; (cite: McLean10a; McLean12a)) on Keck I

question.value: Does a z=1.555 dusty star-forming disk galaxy have a flat or declining outer rotation curve, and what is its dark matter fraction?

evidence.quote: We present an observational counterexample, a galaxy named DSFG850.95 at $z=1.555$ (4.1 Gyr after the big bang) that hosts a flat rotation curve between radii of $\sim$6–14 kpc

evidence.quote: The galaxy, DSFG850.95, was observed in the H band for a total integration time of 1920 s with the slit width set to $0.7\ensuremath{''}$.

evidence.quote: we fit a Sérsic profile (cite: Sersic63a) to H-band imaging of DSFG850.95 from the UltraVISTA survey (cite: McCracken12a).

findings_qualitative.value: No evidence of a velocity turnover with declining rotation; the outer slope is consistent with flat

evidence.quote: There is no evidence of a velocity turnover with declining rotation.

claims.hypothesis: Do z>1 disk galaxies necessarily have declining outer rotation curves?
claims.experiment: Keck/MOSFIRE Halpha rotation curve of DSFG850.95 fitted with modified arctan model
claims.result: c = -0.5±1.0 km/s/arcsec, V_flat = 285±12 km/s over 6–14 kpc
claims.finding: The rotation curve is flat, a counterexample to declining curves

evidence.quote: showing a flat rotation curve between $\sim$6–14 kpc (1.2–2.8 disk scale lengths), well-fit by an arctangent function.

claims.hypothesis: Is the dark matter fraction in the outer galaxy low as at some other z>1 galaxies?
claims.experiment: Combine dynamical mass with stellar mass and ALMA-based gas mass
claims.finding: Dark matter fraction is similar to the Milky Way and low-z disks

evidence.loc: Dynamical, Stellar, Gas, and Dark Matter Masses
evidence.quote: DSFG850.95 has a dark matter fraction closer to that of the Milky Way than the galaxies in (cite: Genzel17a)

limitations_admitted.value: Slit misaligned with the H-band major axis by 23±4 deg, which could underpredict the rotation velocity

evidence.quote: Large misalignments would result in an underprediction of the maximum rotational velocity of a galaxy

referee_caveats_inferred: Single galaxy, so no statistical conclusion
Gas mass depends on Scoville dust-to-gas calibration

missing_for_reproduction: ALMA data processing details and flux

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~10 GB for the ALMA continuum; the MOSFIRE and UltraVISTA data are small
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA is used only for a continuum gas mass, with no processing details; the kinematic methods are described fairly well.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The main results come from Keck data, and the ALMA recipe is incomplete.
